Facts of the case, in brief are that FIR No. RC-DAI-2003 (A)-0063 was registered on 23.12.2003 on the source information that the officials of Conservation Sanitory Engineering Department (CSE), West Zone of Municipal Corporation of Delhi had resorted to illegal means in regularization of employment of casual Safai Karamcharis during the year 2001.

sentences.text: It was alleged that R.K. Lakhra (Sanitory Superintendent), Jeet Ram (Sanitory guard/Beldar) and other unknown officials of MCD showed seven persons (A-2 to A-8) working as casual Safai Karamcharis since 1988 though they never worked in the CSE department, West Zone, MCD.
The said seven persons (A-2 to A-8) were regularized as permanent employees of MCD in the year 2001 on the basis of forged and fabricated documents and were issued appointment letters.
3. It is further alleged in the FIR that in the original seniority list issued by CSE headquaters, the said seven persons (A-2 to A- 8) had not been shown working as casual labourers.
In fact, as per the date of birth of these seven persons (A-2 to A-8) as per record, most of them had not even attained the age of 18 years at RC-DAI-2003-A-0063 CBI vs. JEET RAM & ORS.

These seven persons (A-2 to A-8) were appointed in circle no. 20 of the West Zone, MCD i.e.
Ashok Nagar.

4. On this information, the present FIR under Section 120B, 420, 467 and 468 IPC and Section 13 (2) r/w Section 13 (1) (d), PC Act, 1988 was registered against accused R.K. Lakhra, Jeet Ram, Kunta Devi, Nirmala, Saroj, Sharda Devi, Maya Devi, Satish, Vijendra and other unknown officials of MCD.
During investigation, it was found that in July 1998, CSE HQ, MCD had decided to regularize Daily Wager Safai Karamcharis who were engaged from 01.04.1988 to 31.03.1990 w.e.f 01.04.1995.
The consolidated seniority list of Daily Wagers and Substitute Safai Karamcharis prepared by CSE HQ for the period 1988-90 contained names of 2721 Daily Wagers and 2953 Substitute Safai Karamcharis.
Names of none of the FIR named seven accused persons (A-2 to A-8) figured in the said list.
Similarly, the names of the said seven persons also did not figure in the seniority list of Daily Wagers prepared by CSE, West Zone for the period 1988-1990 that contained around 457 names.
5. The said seven persons (A-2 to A-8) never worked in CSE, West Zone during the period 1987 to 2001.
They started working in CSE, West Zone from April 2001, only after joining as regular Safai Karamcharis.
As per the details mentioned in their service books, all of them were minors in the year 1988.
Thus, the seven accused persons were appointed on the basis of fake Regularization Orders.

sentences.text: During investigation, all seven Safai Karamcharis (A-2 to A-8) were examined; they gave their dates of birth which were different from the date mentioned in their service books.

Investigation further revealed that the dispatch numbers on the office orders issued by CSE HQ does not tally with the dispatch numbers mentioned in the dispatch register; the letter for medical examination was also found to be not issued by CSE HQ; the regularization order and medical request letter were found to be forged and were written by one Ravinder Bharti (working as ASI in CSE Department,
Lajpat Nagar) on the asking of accused Jeet Ram (A-1) at the instance of R.K. Lakhra.

Ravinder Bharti turned approver and in his statement under Section 164 CrPC, he admitted to have written the portions of regularization order at the instance of Jeet Ram who was acting at the instance of R.K. Lakhra.
R.K. Lakhra, in further of the criminal conspiracy, issued joining letters in favour of the seven Safai Karamcharis (A-2 to A-8).
7. Since the acts committed by accused Jeet Ram and Ravinder Bharti were not performed under the colour of their office, sanction for prosecution under Section 19, PC Act was not sought.

However,
since R.K. The said seven persons (A-2 to A-8) were regularized as permanent employees of MCD in the year 2001 on the basis of forged and fabricated documents and were issued appointment letters.
3. It is further alleged in the FIR that in the original seniority list issued by CSE headquaters, the said seven persons (A-2 to A- 8) had not been shown working as casual labourers.
In fact, as per the date of birth of these seven persons (A-2 to A-8) as per record, most of them had not even attained the age of 18 years at RC-DAI-2003-A-0063 CBI vs. JEET RAM & ORS.
These seven persons (A-2 to A-8) were appointed in circle no. 20 of the West Zone, MCD i.e.
Ashok Nagar.
4. On this information, the present FIR under Section 120B, 420, 467 and 468 IPC and Section 13 (2) r/w Section 13 (1) (d), PC Act, 1988 was registered against accused R.K. Lakhra, Jeet Ram, Kunta Devi, Nirmala, Saroj, Sharda Devi, Maya Devi, Satish, Vijendra and other unknown officials of MCD.
5. The said seven persons (A-2 to A-8) never worked in CSE, West Zone during the period 1987 to 2001.
Thus, the seven accused persons were appointed on the basis of fake Regularization Orders.
7. Since the acts committed by accused Jeet Ram and Ravinder Bharti were not performed under the colour of their office, sanction for prosecution under Section 19, PC Act was not sought.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The burden to establish the commission of offence by the accused persons was upon the prosecution.
It is a matter of record that orders regularizing the Safai Karamchari were issued only to the individuals whose names were finalized in the due process in the final seniority list.
46. On scrutinizing the testimony of all the witnesses referred above, it stands established that for regularization of the Safai Karamcharis, two seniority lists Ex.PW1/1 and Ex.PW1/2 were prepared and finalized at CSC by the concerned officer in the discharge of their official duties.
It further stands established that the validity and genuineness of the said seniority lists was never challenged or disputed by the accused persons.
No objection was ever raised by A-2 to A-8 at any time either with their respective west zone or with CSC for omission of their names in the seniority list.
The accused persons did not reveal as to since when they were working as Safai Karamcharis or Substitute Safai Karamcharis in the respective zone.
No muster roll has been placed on record by the accused persons to substantiate their plea that they were working as Safai Karamcharis or Daily Wagers.
The remuneration received for the alleged work done has not been bought on record by the accused.
So much so, the accused persons did not produce any document whatsoever showing their exact date of birth as mentioned in the request for medical documents.
No such affidavit of age is on record.
The accused persons did not disclose their exact date of birth in their statements recoded under Section 313 CrPC.
47.
The prosecution has further established that the Regularization Order Ex. PW10/A (colly)
allegedly issued by PW10 Darshan Lal was found forged and fabricated.

Similarly, signatures of PW10 Darshan Lal on the request for medical examination form were also found forged.
Apparently, all the accused persons had joined the services with MCD on the strength of forged and fabricated Regularization Order which was never in existence.
In the absence of names of A-2 to A-8 in the final seniority list Ex.PW1/1 and Ex.PW1/2,
there was no occasion for the competent authority to issue any Regularization Order qua A-2 to A-8 as none of them was working in the respective zone during the relevant period from 1988 to 1990.
48. All the incriminating evidence appearing against A-2 to A- 8 were put in their statements recorded u/s 313 CrPC.
The verbatim response has been given by all the accused stating that they were not minor at the time of issuance of appointment letters and had submitted affidavits regarding their date of birth.
They had requested the investigating officer to collect the muster roll but it was not collected deliberately and the case was not investigated properly.
None of the accused disclosed their exact date of birth in 313 CrPC statement.
None of the accused claimed if they had joined the services on any particular date in the west zone.
It is also not disclosed if any exact payment for the work done was received.
They also did not explain as to how and what circumstances, the regularization order was issued under the forged signatures of PW10 Darshan Lal.

The evidence of DW1 is of no help to the accused persons, as he did not state that the accused persons were employed with the MCD during the relevant period.
The record produced by DW1 pertains to the period when the accused persons had joined the service in MCD after procuring forged and fabricated regularization order.
From the above discussion, it stands established that the accused persons (A-2 to A-8) were issued letters for medical examination and regularization orders despite the fact that their names did not find mention in the seniority lists of Safai Karamcharis on the basis of which the Safai Karamcharis were regularized.
It has further been established that the request letters for medical examination and the regularization orders in favour of the accused persons (A-2 to A-8) were forged and fabricated.
51. In view of above discussion, the Court is of the view that the prosecution has established that the accused persons (A-2 to A-8) procured forged and fabricated regularization order by making false representations regarding their eligibility and age and used the said forged regularization order to obtain appointment letters as regular Safai Karamcharis.
The accused persons (A-2 to A-8) joined the service with MCD and obtained monetary benefits, wages and other benefits.
The regularization order created a legal right in favour of the accused persons (A-2 to A-8) for appointment as Regular Safai Karamcharis in the MCD and thus, the said regularization orders would fall within the definition of "valuable security" as defined in Section 30, IPC.
52.
Accordingly, the prosecution has led sufficient evidence to bring home the guilt of the accused persons.
